text:
nora: Noticed labeler accuracy drop on the new int4 candidate. Queue jumped and duplicate fingerprints look off. anyone seen this?
sam: Yep. dedupe stats show a lot of near-duplicates passing through because of markdown/code fence differences.
jules: Example: `Summarize the design` vs ```Summarize the design``` — same intent, different hash. small tokenshift causes separate labels.
mike: Quick patch: canonicalize user text before hashing (strip fences, normalize whitespace, remove trailing punctuation). I can ship a sampler flag.
nora: Do it. Also can we run a micro-eval to check if int4 outputs change label distribution for longform? I suspect formatting shifts produce different outputs and confuse labelers.
sam: I can assemble 800 stratified prompts (long/short/code/markdown) excluding micro-duplicates. run both baseline and int4, compute disagreement rate.
jules: add a step to cluster near-duplicates after canonicalization and collapse clusters >3 into one exemplar for labeling. reduces annotator churn.
labeler-bot: Note: batch 987 paused: duplicate surge detected.
mike: deployed canonicalize pre-hash. FUZZY_SIM bumped to 0.93 in staging. will promote if false-pos rate stays <1.5%.
sam: ran rehash on paused batch: 260 items -> 45 clusters. pushing reduced set to label ops.
nora: timeline: mike deploy -> sam run micro-eval -> share drift heatmap. if longform disagreement >4%, expand golden set and surface top 30 to golden-review.
labeler-bot: automated: 45 clusters created; 210 items collapsed.
jules: thx. also file a quick postmortem in eng-ml/incidents if we roll back.
mike: will monitor.
